_comment: Soyara DEX - AgentValidator execution rules. Since v2 these rules are only half the story: the binding constraint is the settlement commitment, which AgentExecutor re-derives from calldata and which only the AgentValidator Intelligent Contract can issue a verdict for.

slippage.description: 300 bps = 3.00% hard cap. 100 bps = 1.00% warning threshold.

amounts.description: Soft USD cap for UI display. Executor enforces on-chain.

deadline.description: Proposals must not be expired. Executor enforces on-chain.

llm_review_policy.prompt_injection_protection: Only structured numeric/enum fields are passed to LLM. User free-text is NEVER included.
llm_review_policy.description: LLM is a secondary coherence check. Deterministic rules run first and are authoritative.

security_notes: Never allow arbitrary calldata to reach the executor
All token addresses must be in the approved list
All router addresses must be in the approved list
LLM prompt never contains user-supplied free-text
Contract can be paused by owner in emergencies

fee.description: Fee and fee collector are consensus-governed parameters bound into the settlement commitment. Previously neither was hashed nor checked, so a settlement agent could route the input to any address at any rate the entrypoint accepted - up to 100%. AgentExecutor enforces its own cap independently (maxFeeBps, hard ceiling 500).

quote.description: Validators decode the aggregator route program, confirm every pool against the V2/V3 factory, and re-derive the output from live reserves; the declared quote must match within tolerance_bps. minAmountOut must sit one slippage band below that verified quote, and the verdict expires after verdict_ttl_seconds so a quote checked against live pools cannot be settled long after those pools have moved.

settlement.mechanism: IC external message -> ghost contract handleOp() -> AgentExecutor.recordVerdict
settlement.description: The settlement agent is a relayer. It cannot create an approval: recordVerdict is gated on msg.sender being the validator IC, which no operator key can produce.
